tasks.title: [Claude x Jules production PRD-001] carrier blob SHA test must ignore CRLF checkouts
tasks.body:
Task for Jules: Claude x Jules production campaign PRD-C1, task PRD-001 (a small real bug fix with a regression test).

**Bug.** `automation/command_bus/tests/test_claude_jules_dispatch_contract.py::PinnedCarrierTests::test_vendored_carrier_validators_match_pinned_blob_shas` computes a git blob SHA from the raw bytes of each vendored carrier file. On a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` the working tree has CRLF line endings, git itself stores LF, so the test fails on Windows only. Observed on main `702497c` with Windows Python: `jules_api_request.py` gives `6db9d48...` instead of the pinned `1aebad3...`. On Linux the test passes.

**Fix.** In that test file only, compute the blob SHA from the file content with CRLF normalized to LF (what git stores), using a small helper function. Keep comparing against the same pinned SHAs. Do not change `jules_carrier_current.PINNED_BLOB_SHA`, the vendored carrier files, or any production code.

**Regression test.** Add a test in the same file that shows: the helper gives the same SHA for `b"a
b
"` and `b"a
b
"`; that SHA equals git's blob SHA of the LF content (`hashlib.sha1(b"blob %d�" % len(data) + data)` on the LF bytes); and different content gives a different SHA.

Change only `automation/command_bus/tests/test_claude_jules_dispatch_contract.py`. Do not weaken, skip or delete any existing test. Run the test commands below before opening the pull request, and put `Fixes #<this issue>` in the pull request body.

tasks.title: [Claude x Jules production PRD-002] sf8 authority test must read files as UTF-8
tasks.body:
Task for Jules: Claude x Jules production campaign PRD-C2, task PRD-002 (a small real bug fix with a regression test).

**Bug.** `automation/command_bus/tests/test_sf8_authority_issuer_candidate.py` reads files with `Path.read_text()` without an encoding (module level: the candidate workflow and the control tower registry; and in `test_no_other_workflow_uses_authority_profile`). On Windows the default encoding is cp932, and a workflow file contains UTF-8 text, so the test module errors on Windows only. Observed on main `702497c` with Windows Python: `UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp932' codec can't decode byte 0x92`. With `PYTHONUTF8=1` the same tests pass. On Linux they pass.

**Fix.** In that test file only, pass `encoding="utf-8"` to every `read_text()` call. Keep every assertion and regex exactly as it is.

**Regression test.** Add a test in the same file that reads every workflow file the module scans with `encoding="utf-8"` and asserts each is decodable and non-empty, and a test that asserts the module's file reads name an explicit encoding (for example by checking the source of the module with `ast`, so a bare `read_text()` cannot come back unnoticed).

Change only `automation/command_bus/tests/test_sf8_authority_issuer_candidate.py`. Do not weaken, skip or delete any existing test. Run the test commands below before opening the pull request, and put `Fixes #<this issue>` in the pull request body.
